===Etymology 1===
{{dercat|en|gem-pro}}
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:beggen|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|beggen}}, of uncertain origin. Possibly from {{der|en|ang||*becgian, *bedcian}}, {{glossary|syncopated}} forms of {{m|ang|bedecian||to beg}}, itself of {{unk|en|title=obscure}} origin. Possibly from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*bedukōn}}, a frequentative verb derived from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*bedu}} (“plea, petition, prayer”, whence {{m+|en|bead}}). Alternatively from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*bedagō|t=petitioner, requester, beggar}}, an agent noun from the same source. Compare {{cog|frr|bēdagi|t=to pray}}, {{cog|got|𐌱𐌹𐌳𐌰𐌲𐍅𐌰|t=beggar}}. All ultimately from the root of {{m+|en|bid}}, which see for more. An alternative theory considers the verb a backformation from {{m|en|beggar}} and derives the latter from {{der|en|fro|begart|t=kind of lay brother}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[request#Verb|request]] the [[help#Noun|help]] of someone, often in the form of [[money]].
#: {{ux|en|He '''begged''' on the street corner from passers-by.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[plead]] with someone for [[help]], a [[favor#Noun|favor]], etc.; to [[entreat]].
#: {{synonyms|en|supplicate}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''beg''' your pardon. I didn’t mean to cause offence.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''begged''' her to go to the prom with him.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|I|iii|passage=you do '''beg''' your good will in this case.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|27|58|passage=[Joseph] '''begged''' the body of Jesus.}}
#* {{RQ:Falkner Moonfleet|year=1934|passage=But that same day came Sam Tewkesbury to the Why Not? about nightfall, and '''begged''' a glass of rum, being, as he said, 'all of a shake' [...]}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[unwillingly]] [[provoke]] a [[negative]], often [[violent]], [[reaction]].
#: {{ux|en|The way you keep eating raw meat, you're just '''begging''' to get tapeworms.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|or|intransitive}} To [[obviously]] [[lack]] or be [[in need of]] something.
#: {{ux|en|A captivating novel that just '''begs''' for a movie adaptation}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} ''In the phrase'' ''{{l|en|beg the question}}'': to [[assume]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|proscribed}} ''In the phrase'' ''{{l|en|beg the question}}'': to [[raise#Verb|raise]] (a [[question#Noun|question]]).
#: {{antonyms|en|set aside}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|law|obsolete}} To ask to be [[appoint]]ed [[guardian]] for, or to ask to have a guardian appointed for.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1612|author={{w|John Harington (writer)|John Harington}}|title=Epigrams
|passage=Else some will '''beg''' thee, in the court of wards.}}

=====Usage notes=====
This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''to [[infinitive]]''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]]

====Noun====

# The act of begging; an [[implore|imploring]] request.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Cathy Gohlke|title=William Henry is a Fine Name/I Have Seen Him in the Watchfires Set|passage=“Lord,” I prayed, “it's a long time since I came to You for anything besides a quick '''beg''' for help. And it seems every time I come to You I'm asking something bigger, more impossible. But I'm here again. {{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|UK|slang|derogatory}} A [[pretentious]], [[attention-seeking]], or [[eccentric]] person.
#*: Girls told me about not wanting to be seen by boys as "too much", "too loud", "weird", "annoying", a "pick me", or "a '''beg'''" (someone looking for attention). They told me how boys can be loud and funny, but that girls had better not.
